title: Dry January
paragraphs: In Britain, it's bottoms up from the week before Christmas till the last firework explodes in the sky announcing the new year. The last Friday before Christmas - popularly known as 'Mad Friday' - is one of the busiest periods for the country's pubs and clubs.

But it's not just the bars that get busy. Ambulances and A&E departments around Britain get packed out too. Head injuries, cuts, falls... it's easy to end up hurting yourself or others when inhibitions and composure disappear and your head is spinning due to alcohol. Revellers have been warned by the health authorities about the dangers of excessive drinking but indulgence seems to be part of the festivities for some.
The charity Alcohol Concern is running a campaign of abstinence by encouraging people to have a dry January.

Jackie Ballard, the charity's Chief Executive, believes the initiative has been successful in recent years. She says: "More than two-thirds of people even six months later are drinking at reduced levels having had a month off booze. But also a study has shown the impact it has on people's health reducing their blood pressure and blood sugar levels."

The study by the University of Sussex followed up nearly 900 participants in Alcohol Concern's Dry January campaign and found out that 72% of them had kept harmful drinking sessions down and 4% were still not drinking. Fears that a booze-free month would cause people to binge drink the next month didn't materialise.

Moderation seems to be the key to everything. The official recommendation for women is not to regularly drink more than 2 to 3 units of alcohol a day. That's no more than a 175ml glass of 13% ABV wine. The limit for men is 3 to 4 units of alcohol - no more than a pint of 5.2% ABV lager, beer or cider.

vocabulary.entry: bottoms up [phr.] /'bɒtəmz ʌp/ 干杯 (固定搭配；口语)
vocabulary.example: They raised their glasses and cried 'Bottoms up!'
vocabulary.translation: 他们举杯喊道“干杯！”

vocabulary.entry: Mad Friday [n.] /mæd 'fraɪdeɪ/ 疯狂星期五 (专有名词；口语)
vocabulary.example: Mad Friday is known as one of the busiest nights of the year for pubs and clubs.
vocabulary.translation: 疯狂星期五被认为是酒吧和俱乐部一年中最繁忙的夜晚之一。

vocabulary.entry: A&E department [n.] /eɪ ənd iː dɪ'pɑːtmənt/ 急诊室 (专业词汇；缩写)
vocabulary.example: She was taken to the A&E department after collapsing at work.
vocabulary.translation: 她在工作中晕倒后被送往急诊室。

vocabulary.entry: head injuries [n. pl.] /hed 'ɪndʒəriz/ 头部受伤 (单数: head injury)
vocabulary.example: Wearing a helmet greatly reduces the risk of serious head injuries.
vocabulary.translation: 佩戴头盔可以大大降低严重头部受伤的风险。

vocabulary.entry: inhibitions [n. pl.] /ˌɪnhɪˈbɪʃənz/ 克制；拘谨 (单数: inhibition)
vocabulary.example: She lost her inhibitions after a couple of glasses of wine.
vocabulary.translation: 几杯葡萄酒下肚后，她不再拘谨。

vocabulary.entry: composure [n.] /kəmˈpəʊʒə/ 镇静；沉着 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: He maintained his composure throughout the difficult interview.
vocabulary.translation: 在整个艰难的面试过程中他始终保持镇定。

vocabulary.entry: revellers [n. pl.] /ˈrevələz/ 狂欢者 (单数: reveller)
vocabulary.example: New Year's Eve revellers filled the city centre streets.
vocabulary.translation: 新年前夜的狂欢者挤满了市中心的街道。

vocabulary.entry: excessive drinking [n.] /ɪkˈsesɪv ˈdrɪŋkɪŋ/ 过度饮酒 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Excessive drinking can lead to serious health problems.
vocabulary.translation: 过度饮酒会导致严重的健康问题。

vocabulary.entry: indulgence [n.] /ɪnˈdʌldʒəns/ 放纵；沉溺 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: His health suffered from years of indulgence in rich food and drink.
vocabulary.translation: 多年沉溺于油腻饮食和饮酒损害了他的健康。

vocabulary.entry: abstinence [n.] /ˈæbstɪnəns/ 戒除；节制 (专业词汇；书面语)
vocabulary.example: The doctor recommended total abstinence from alcohol.
vocabulary.translation: 医生建议完全戒酒。

vocabulary.entry: dry January [n.] /draɪ dʒænˈjuəri/ 一月戒酒 (固定搭配；专有名词)
vocabulary.example: Many people take part in Dry January to give their liver a rest.
vocabulary.translation: 许多人参加“一月戒酒”活动让肝脏休息一下。

vocabulary.entry: booze [n.] /buːz/ 酒 (口语词汇)
vocabulary.example: He's been off the booze for three weeks now.
vocabulary.translation: 他已经戒酒三周了。

vocabulary.entry: blood pressure [n.] /blʌd ˈpreʃə/ 血压 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise can help to lower your blood pressure.
vocabulary.translation: 定期锻炼有助于降低血压。

vocabulary.entry: blood sugar levels [n. pl.] /blʌd ˈʃʊɡə ˈlevəlz/ 血糖水平 (单数: blood sugar level；专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: A healthy diet helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.
vocabulary.translation: 健康的饮食有助于维持稳定的血糖水平。

vocabulary.entry: binge drink [v.] /bɪndʒ drɪŋk/ 酗酒；狂饮 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Young people are being warned not to binge drink at parties.
vocabulary.translation: 年轻人被警告不要在派对上酗酒。

vocabulary.entry: moderation [n.] /ˌmɒdəˈreɪʃən/ 适度；节制 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Alcohol should be consumed in moderation.
vocabulary.translation: 饮酒应当适量。

vocabulary.entry: units of alcohol [n. pl.] /ˈjuːnɪts əv ˈælkəhɒl/ 酒精单位 (单数: unit of alcohol；专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: A standard glass of wine contains about two units of alcohol.
vocabulary.translation: 一杯标准葡萄酒含有约两个酒精单位。

vocabulary.entry: ABV [n.] /ˌeɪ biː ˈviː/ 酒精含量 (专业词汇；缩写)
vocabulary.example: This beer has an ABV of 5 percent.
vocabulary.translation: 这种啤酒的酒精含量为5%。

vocabulary.entry: lager [n.] /ˈlɑːɡə/ 拉格啤酒 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: He ordered a pint of lager at the pub.
vocabulary.translation: 他在酒吧点了一品脱拉格啤酒。

vocabulary.entry: cider [n.] /ˈsaɪdə/ 苹果酒
vocabulary.example: She prefers cider to beer because it's sweeter.
vocabulary.translation: 比起啤酒她更喜欢苹果酒，因为它更甜。

sentences.chinese: 苏塞克斯大学的研究跟踪了“酒精关注”的“1月戒酒”活动中近900名参与者，发现72%的人减少了有害饮酒，4%的人仍然不喝酒。

sentences.chinese: 人们担心戒酒一个月会导致下个月酗酒的情况并未发生。

sentences.chinese: 适度似乎是一切的关键。

sentences.chinese: 官方建议女性不要经常饮用每天超过2到3单位的酒精。

sentences.english: That's no more than a 175ml glass of 13% ABV wine.
sentences.chinese: 也就是不超过一杯175毫升、酒精含量为13%的葡萄酒。
